reason: The quote states storage classes are configured at the object level and one general purpose bucket can hold objects in all storage classes except S3 Express One Zone.

Under the S3 Storage Lens paragraph, the quote says you can identify buckets without Lifecycle rules to abort incomplete multipart uploads older than 7 days, and buckets not following data-protection practices such as Replication or Versioning.
The quote lists the same six free metric categories: summary, cost optimization, data protection, access management, performance and event metrics.
The quote states free and advanced tiers, the advanced tier at additional charge, and lists the same five advanced features including CloudWatch publishing and contextual recommendations.

The FAQ quotes state organization-wide visibility into usage and activity, daily organization level recommendations for cost efficiency and data protection, and that S3 Inventory lists objects and metadata for a bucket or shared prefix for object-level analysis.
The quote states strong read-after-write consistency for PUT and DELETE of objects in all AWS Regions, for new objects, overwrites and deletes.

The quotes name the four bucket types, state table buckets store tabular data in Apache Iceberg format queryable by Athena, Redshift and Spark, and vector buckets store and query vectors with dedicated API operations.
The quotes state you must use the bucket-name.s3-accelerate.amazonaws.com endpoint, regular endpoints remain for standard transfer, and the bucket name must be DNS-compliant without periods.
The quote states a bucket-level feature for fast transfers over long distances to a general purpose bucket, using CloudFront edge locations and an optimized network path to S3.
The quote and its context state that on each accelerated upload AWS checks speed and, if not likely faster than a regular transfer to the same Region, does not charge and may bypass the system.
The FAQ quote states the same security as regular transfers, standard TCP with no firewall changes, and that no data is ever saved at edge locations.
The quote states acceleration between the client and a single bucket, pricing based on the edge location used, and pricing in addition to Data Transfer pricing.
The quote says Transfer Acceleration is the better choice if higher throughput is desired and to consider CloudFront PUT/POST for objects or data sets under 1 GB.
The three quotes are the three listed reasons: central bucket uploads from all over the world, GB to TB across continents regularly, and unused available bandwidth.
The quotes recommend regularly checking Trusted Advisor security advisories and in particular warnings about buckets with open access permissions.
The quotes state one UpdateObjectEncryption job supports a manifest of up to 20 billion objects and the operation can change the customer managed KMS key.
The quotes state no support for unencrypted, DSSE-KMS or SSE-C objects, SSE-S3 cannot be specified, and the operation fails on objects with an Object Lock retention mode or legal hold.
The quotes state an existing key in a versioning-enabled bucket gets another version, buckets hold an unlimited number of objects, and write permission is needed to upload.
The quote supports unique version IDs and null for pre-existing objects; the last clause (a later overwrite gets a unique version ID) is only in the context sentence, not in the quote.
The quote states only the bucket owner or an authorized IAM user can permanently delete a version, and a DELETE with versionId deletes it permanently without a delete marker.
The quote states normal S3 rates apply to every version stored or requested; an older stored version being billed follows directly, as the FAQ example under the same heading shows.
The quotes state the delete marker becomes the current version, a GET then returns 404 Not Found, and a GET with a noncurrent version ID still returns that version.
The quote states versioning is enabled and suspended at the bucket level and a version-enabled bucket can never return to unversioned, only be suspended.
The quotes state new versions are created only on PUT, CopyObject works via PUT, and changing tags does not create a new version.
The quote states S3 Versioning is disabled on buckets by default and must be explicitly enabled.

The FAQ quotes state existing objects are preserved on PUT, POST, COPY or DELETE, GET returns the most recent version, after DELETE simple requests no longer retrieve the object but versions remain, and only the owner can permanently delete a version.

The quotes support the rollback window and deleting noncurrent versions after N days with at least N newer versions; the archive-to-cheaper-class-then-delete example appears only in the context, not in a quote.
The quotes state suspending stops accruing new versions and existing objects do not change; only handling of future requests changes.
The quote states the versioning state applies to all (never some) objects in the bucket; the three states are listed directly above it.

The quotes state the endpoint is a logical entity allowing connectivity only to S3 that helps keep traffic off the open internet, bucket policies can control which VPCs or endpoints have access, and a VPC without an internet gateway helps prevent exfiltration.
The quotes state a private connection not requiring internet, VPN, NAT instance or Direct Connect, connectivity only to S3, routing-only change, and public endpoints continue to work.

The quote supports block storage being direct-attached with low-latency access for fast and consistent I/O; it does not name Amazon EBS and does not state that object storage is not attached to an instance.
The quote supports file storage mountable over NFS and SMB for shared data across instances; it does not name EFS or FSx and does not state that object storage is not mounted as a file system.
The quote says to review bucket policies regularly, avoid public buckets unless absolutely necessary, and consider AWS Config to detect public buckets and CloudFront to serve S3 content.

The quote states default and service-controlled keys are managed and used by AWS, customer managed keys for sensitive data needing fine-grained key access, with full control including rotation and key policies.
The security pillar quote states S3 now encrypts all new objects by default with no impact on performance.
The quote states IAM Access Analyzer can analyze S3 buckets and generate findings when an S3 policy grants access to an external entity.
The quotes say to map keys to data classifications to avoid over-permissive single-key use, with the example of separate KMS keys for production and development or test data.
The quote states Object Lock prevents deletion or overwrite even by the root user until the lock expires, and Glacier Vault Lock offers a similar feature for Glacier archives.
The quote says to use S3 Inventory to audit and report on replication and encryption status for business, compliance and regulatory needs.
